notes:
Summary: Inbound SMB devtool startup building a context-heavy code assistant. Self-serve sign-up, quickly moved to discovery. Wants hosted API (public cloud/AWS) for time-to-market. Primary ask: reliable long-window completions (30k+ tokens), predictable cost and clear rate-limit semantics for concurrent editors.

Key technical constraints / asks:
- Long context: will stream large repo+session context into calls; worried about token cost and latency at 20k-40k active window. Wants guidance on prefix/KV caching to avoid re-sending full context every request.
- Rate limits: editors generate spikes (30–60 rps in short bursts during team syncs). Needs clear burst handling and retry behavior; asked about token-based vs requests-per-minute policies. "Can we get deterministic 429 behavior and guidance for backoff?"
- SDKs: strong ask for TypeScript-first examples (Node + Deno), official streaming client that supports incremental partial tokens and reconnection/resume. Also wants python client for backend batch rerank jobs.
- Observability: token-level cost reporting per-call, per-route dashboards would be a huge benefit. Interested in per-route latency histograms and sample traces.
- Security: SSO/SAML needed likely in Q3; audit logs and simple KMS integration is a plus but not blocking for initial POC.

Sales notes / quotes:
- CTO (via call): "We need an API that doesn't surprise us on cost when we turn up context."
- PM: "If your SDKs make streaming and resume trivial, we can prototype in 48 hours."

POC plan proposed by AE/SE:
1) Provide sandbox hosted_api keys + $500 credit for two weeks.
2) Run a 48–72 hour throughput test: simulate editor burst patterns (30–60 rps) with 20k token contexts, measure p95 latency and any 429s.
3) Provide a short integration guide: TypeScript streaming example, Python batch reranker snippet, recommended batching/cache params.

Current blockers: not enough clarity on rate_limit semantics and per-token pricing for long-window usage. Customer asked for a short cost-estimate template for a 10-engineer team at expected qps.

Next steps owner: Marissa to provision sandbox and coordinate with Diego on test harness. Customer target: decide on hosted-api POC within 2 weeks, move to evaluation if test passes.
